title: Humanity Created by God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Humanity created by God means that human life begins with the Creator’s intentional design, ownership, and purpose. People are not accidents, machines, or self-made beings; they exist because God made them for Himself.
summary: Humanity created by God means that human life begins with the Creator’s intentional design, ownership, and purpose. People are not accidents, machines, or self-made beings; they exist because God made them for Himself.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the eternal Son through whom all things were made and the true man who restores humanity to God’s purpose. In Him, created people learn both their dependence on God and their hope of redemption.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Humanity begins with God’s creative act. People do not define their own origin, value, or purpose apart from Him. Scripture teaches that God made mankind and breathed life into man, so every human life stands before the Creator.

Being created by God means human beings are dependent creatures. Life, breath, time, strength, place, and purpose come from Him. Human autonomy is never ultimate because people belong to the One who made them.

This doctrine also gives human life meaning. People are not cosmic accidents or disposable bodies. They were made to know God, worship Him, steward His creation, live under His authority, and reflect His glory.

Sin has damaged humanity’s response to the Creator, but it has not erased God’s claim over His creatures. The Gospel calls created people back to the God who made them and restores them through Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A person who does not know where life comes from will struggle to understand why life matters. This doctrine anchors human worth and responsibility in God’s creative will rather than in culture, ability, status, or feeling.

It also confronts pride and despair. Pride says, “I belong to myself.” Despair says, “My life has no purpose.” Scripture answers both by declaring that humanity belongs to the Creator who made people for His glory and can restore them through Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive your life as a gift from God, not as something self-owned or meaningless. Worship the Creator, steward your body and days before Him, and treat every person as one made by God. Let the truth of creation lead you to humility, gratitude, obedience, and hope in Christ.
